findings.message: the pattern matches 4 of 5 sample lines. It must match every one: a line it misses is dropped entirely, not partly parsed. The first it misses is '[12] Oct 25 15:14:25 Login attempt for nonexistent user from 172.21.55.93:55370'. Of the 7 patterns, the closest to it is '^\\[%{INT:pid}\\] (?<timestamp>%{MONTH} +%{MONTHDAY} %{TIME}) Child connection from %{IP:client_ip}:%{INT:client_port}$'. the pattern matches up to %{IP:client_ip}, which fails on '] Oct 25 15:14:25 Login attempt for none'. The capture before it, %{INT:pid}, matched only '12' and stopped at '] Oct 25 15:' - it is too narrow, and that is the one to widen. That position does not hold a bare number If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.
